propositions: RemoteRef.instance is never populated in production code; it must be constructed from the configured base URL and injected at backend creation time via a new pure helper that normalises scheme, case, ports, and trailing slashes

Backend protocol does not declare remote_ref() as a port member, though FakeBackend has implemented it since J7, leaving a gap where contract tests run against a fake strictly more capable than production

RemoteRef.instance does not prevent local-id collision between two same-vendor deployments because _jira_key_to_local_id derives ids from the Jira key alone, and vendor already separates Cloud from DC
The remote_ref() method must resolve no configuration at call time; instance values must arrive via constructor parameters passed by build_backend factories that already hold resolved settings
Two deployments with different base URLs must yield unequal RemoteRef values for the same remote_id, and equivalent URL spellings must normalize to the same instance value
Both ADRs 0055 and 0035 must be amended to correct the claim that instance prevents local-id collision and clarify that this story does not persist RemoteRef anywhere
